title: Mexico threatens to kick players off World Cup team in latest spat with Liga MX clubs
content:
The Mexico Football Federation (FMF) has warned Liga MX players that they will be left off the final 2026 World Cup squad if they do not report to a pre-planned World Cup camp on May 6, despite it taking place outside of a designated FIFA international window and during some of the most important matches on the club calendar. In a Wednesday morning press release, the FMF said that per the national team staff’s direction “any player who does not turn up at the (national team’s) training center will miss the World Cup.”

This stems from an April 28 statement in which the FMF announced that 20 Liga MX-based players would take part in a mini pre-World Cup camp in Mexico City beginning Wednesday. Twelve of those players were guaranteed a World Cup squad place, according to an FMF spokesperson at the time. That would mean that players from Toluca and Chivas de Guadalajara called in by manager Javier Aguirre would miss everything from the second leg of the quarterfinals and on in the Liga MX playoffs in addition to the Concacaf Champions Cup semifinal second leg and final.

On Tuesday, Toluca officials asked the FMF to grant the release of players Alexis Vega and Jesus Gallardo for the club’s Champions Cup semifinal decider against LAFC. Toluca is down 2-1 on aggregate after losing the first leg in Los Angeles (and the winner will advance to face Tigres UANL, which ousted Nashville SC 2-0 on aggregate Tuesday night). The ask by Toluca was deemed as a breach of the agreement that FMF had made with Liga MX clubs.

Meanwhile, Chivas faces Tigres in the Liga MX playoffs this Saturday, the second leg of a quarterfinal that Tigres leads 3-1 on aggregate. Club president Amaury Vergara responded on social media platform X late on Tuesday by writing, “The agreement is valid only when all parties respect it. I have instructed the club’s sporting leadership that our players are to report to the club’s facilities tomorrow.” The conflict impacts five Chivas players: former U.S. international midfielder Brian Gutiérrez, versatile veteran Luis Romo, winger Roberto Alvarado, forward Armando González and presumed starting World Cup goalkeeper Raúl Rangel.

FMF’s authoritative declaration on Wednesday now puts several players from Chivas and Toluca, who are otherwise expected to be part of Mexico’s World Cup squad, in a difficult position. Either they play with the clubs in May or play for their country this summer, but not both.

Coincidentally, FMF and Liga MX recently announced a new organizational structure that is intended to allow the domestic league to function as an independent entity. It hasn’t taken long for that autonomy to be tested.

Mexico is a cohosts of the World Cup along with the United States and Canada and will host the opening game when it faces South Africa at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City on June 11.

Aguirre’s final roster is expected to be announced June 1, after friendlies against Ghana and Australia but before a final tournament tune-up against Serbia on June 4.

Mexico’s manager spoke for about seven minutes to the press on Wednesday in the aftermath of the federation’s statement and did anything but soften his stance. Instead, he doubled down.

“I want to tell everyone here that today is a great day,” he said. “Today marks the beginning of the World Cup for us. We’re very excited that this day has come. The (20) players have been called up. They’ll have dinner together tonight.

“As you all were able to deduce, our press release was clear: if a player does not report to camp, he’ll be out of the World Cup. We cannot be flexible in that regard. I want to thank the clubs and the owners who supported this plan, one we presented a long time ago, and that was approved. This is a pact. A project that has not been broken. I want to thank Toluca and Chivas, notably Chivas that is impacted by the number of players (called up). And Toluca a club that is competing in an international tournament. They’re helping us. They’re helping the national team.

“The pact has not been broken. The (Liga MX) playoffs will be played without national team players. For now, we’re all aligned with the conditions that we agreed to.

“I want point out that this is not the first time that the playoffs have taken place without national team players. It has happened many times. I was a coach once when it occurred. And I’ll also point out that Uzbekistan started their (World Cup) camp yesterday. Australia started their camp with eight players. Uzbekistan has players from Manchester City and Leicester. So again, the World Cup has begun. I’m excited about it.

“I want to thank the players for their commitment to the project. (Tijuana’s) Gilberto Mora is already here, training and getting ready. I believe the pride of playing for Mexico has been restored. Playing for Mexico during a World Cup on home soil is priceless.”
